accepted_examples.german: Tom saß am Fenster und las ein Buch.
accepted_examples.english: Tom sat by the window, reading a book.
accepted_examples.note: The book example and translation match the common printed-book sense.

accepted_examples.german: Da er nicht auf seine Gesundheit geachtet hatte, wurde er krank.
accepted_examples.english: Not being careful of his health, he fell ill.
accepted_examples.note: The sentence uses krank as the result of becoming ill; the translation is consistent.

accepted_examples.german: Bist du sicher, dass der Mann Arzt ist?
accepted_examples.english: Are you sure that man is a doctor?
accepted_examples.note: Arzt is used as a predicate noun meaning doctor.

accepted_examples.german: Es sind gar keine Autos auf der Straße.
accepted_examples.english: There are no cars on the street.
accepted_examples.note: Straße is used for a street and the English translation matches.

accepted_examples.german: Der Lehrer erklärte (mir) die quadratische Gleichung sehr gut.
accepted_examples.english: The teacher explained the quadratic equation (to me) very well.
accepted_examples.note: Erklären is used with a direct object and the translation preserves the meaning.

accepted_examples.german: Schicke diese Nachricht so vielen Leuten wie möglich.
accepted_examples.english: Send this message to as many people as you can.
accepted_examples.note: Nachricht is used for a message sent to other people.

accepted_examples.german: Ich muss noch ein paar Briefe schreiben.
accepted_examples.english: I have letters I need to write.
accepted_examples.note: Schreiben is used for writing letters; the English is idiomatic.

accepted_examples.german: Wo finde ich ein Krankenhaus?
accepted_examples.english: Where can I find a hospital?
accepted_examples.note: The sentence asks where to find a hospital; it matches Krankenhaus.

accepted_examples.german: Was hast du außerdem dort getan?
accepted_examples.english: What else did you do there?
accepted_examples.note: Außerdem means in addition or what else in this question.

accepted_examples.german: Ich sagte ihnen, sie sollen mir ein neues Ticket schicken.
accepted_examples.english: I told them to send me another ticket.
accepted_examples.note: Schicken is used for sending a replacement ticket; the translation matches.

accepted_examples.german: Er kann nicht lesen.
accepted_examples.english: He doesn't know how to read.
accepted_examples.note: Lesen is used in the common ability sense; the translation is a natural paraphrase.

accepted_examples.german: Der Ball flog durch die Luft.
accepted_examples.english: The ball flew through the air.
accepted_examples.note: Fliegen is used for movement through the air; the English matches.

accepted_examples.german: Tom muss dich sehr lieben.
accepted_examples.english: Tom must love you very much.
accepted_examples.note: Lieben is used in the common affection sense; the modal must is preserved in English.

accepted_examples.german: Der März ist der dritte Monat des Jahres.
accepted_examples.english: March is the third month of the year.
accepted_examples.note: Monat is used for a calendar month and the translation is exact.

accepted_examples.german: Ich geriet plötzlich in große Sorge.
accepted_examples.english: I was suddenly very worried.
accepted_examples.note: Plötzlich means suddenly; both sentences convey sudden worry.

accepted_examples.german: Dieser alte französische Tisch ist ein sehr wertvolles Möbelstück.
accepted_examples.english: This old French table is a very valuable piece of furniture.
accepted_examples.note: Tisch is used for a table and the translation matches.

accepted_examples.german: Meine Frau ruft mich oft an, wenn ich im Ausland unterwegs bin.
accepted_examples.english: My wife often telephones me when I'm traveling in another country.
accepted_examples.note: Unterwegs describes traveling in another country; the translation is consistent.

accepted_examples.german: Tom ist jetzt mit Johns Exfrau verheiratet.
accepted_examples.english: Tom is now married to John's ex-wife.
accepted_examples.note: Verheiratet is correctly used with mit and the dative person.

accepted_examples.german: Wären Sie so freundlich, das Fenster zu öffnen?
accepted_examples.english: Would you mind opening the window?
accepted_examples.note: Fenster is used as the object of öffnen; the polite request matches.

accepted_examples.german: Die Orange schmeckte weder süß noch sauer.
accepted_examples.english: The orange didn't taste either sweet or sour.
accepted_examples.note: Süß is contrasted with sauer as a taste adjective; translation matches.

accepted_examples.german: Jedenfalls ist das nicht deine Sache.
accepted_examples.english: In any case, it's none of your business.
accepted_examples.note: Jedenfalls is correctly translated as in any case.

accepted_examples.german: Die Akustik in diesem Raum ist ausgezeichnet.
accepted_examples.english: The acoustics in this space are excellent.
accepted_examples.note: Raum means room or space in this acoustic context; translation is accurate.

accepted_examples.german: Viele, die bisher viel Geld für Unterhaltungszwecke ausgegeben haben, müssen jetzt mehr auf ihr Geld achtgeben.
accepted_examples.english: A lot of people who have up until now been spending money having a good time now need to be more careful with their money.
accepted_examples.note: Bisher means up to now; the long sentence and translation convey the same time period.

accepted_examples.german: Die Stadt ist mit dem Zug erreichbar.
accepted_examples.english: The town is accessible by rail.
accepted_examples.note: Zug is used for rail transport; accessible by rail is an accurate English rendering.

accepted_examples.german: Ich habe keine Sekunde lang an dir gezweifelt.
accepted_examples.english: I didn't doubt you for a second.
accepted_examples.note: Sekunde is used for the duration of one second; translation matches.

accepted_examples.german: Das ist nicht das, wofür du es hältst.
accepted_examples.english: It's not what you think it is.
accepted_examples.note: Wofür introduces a relative clause and the translation preserves the intended sense.

accepted_examples.german: Wir freuen uns sehr, dass du hier bist.
accepted_examples.english: We're so glad to have you here.
accepted_examples.note: Freuen is used reflexively in the sense of being glad; the translation is idiomatic.

accepted_examples.german: Er starb, und seine Seele fuhr zur Hölle.
accepted_examples.english: He died and his soul went to hell.
accepted_examples.note: Seele is used in its soul sense; the sentence and translation match.

accepted_examples.german: Hast du Tom schon einmal einen Brief geschrieben?
accepted_examples.english: Have you ever written a letter to Tom?
accepted_examples.note: Brief is used for a written message; the German dative recipient and English translation align.

accepted_examples.german: Er gab mir die Schuld für den Unfall.
accepted_examples.english: He blamed me for the accident.
accepted_examples.note: Unfall is used for an accident and the translation matches.

accepted_examples.german: Setz dich nicht dahin. Das ist Toms Stuhl.
accepted_examples.english: Don't sit there. That's Tom's chair.
accepted_examples.note: Dahin indicates the target place to sit; the English there is a natural rendering.

accepted_examples.german: Sie sagten, dass die Anzahl der Kontrollen erhöht werden sollte.
accepted_examples.english: They said inspections should be increased.
accepted_examples.note: Kontrolle appears in the plural Kontrollen but the sentence clearly illustrates the inspection/check sense.

held_examples.reason: Replaced archaic spelling Verlaß with current Verlass while retaining the idiomatic trust construction.

held_examples.reason: Corrected the translation to preserve musste (had to) and irgendwo (somewhere).

held_examples.german: Was sollten wir Ihrer Meinung nach tun?

held_examples.german: Ist es unbedingt notwendig, daß ich das tue?

held_examples.german: Es gibt keinen Beweis, daß Tom es war.

editorial_examples.german: Meiner Meinung nach ist das keine gute Idee.

editorial_examples.english: That was not an easy decision.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced an overly long, dated sentence and awkward translation with a concise example of Entscheidung.
Corrected the source translation: Arm means arm, not hand.

editorial_examples.german: Im Sommer ist es hier sehr heiß.
editorial_examples.english: It is very hot here in summer.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a sentence whose English wording did not match the German past-tense statement and included an unusually high temperature.

editorial_examples.german: Du musst unbedingt diese Ausstellung sehen.
editorial_examples.english: You absolutely must see this exhibition.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced an example with obsolete spelling with a current, direct example of unbedingt.

editorial_examples.english: There is no proof of that.
